evidence_items.finding: 14 of 62 managed properties were lost in twelve months — a departure rate of approximately 23% of the prior portfolio
evidence_items.rationale: 23% property departure rate in twelve months is a critical adverse retention signal. customer_retention; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: owner attributes all 14 departures to landlords selling investment properties without systematic exit analysis
evidence_items.rationale: Accepting owner-attributed departure reasons without systematic analysis is a critical adverse process maturity signal. process_maturity; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: 18 new properties were won in the same period, producing a net gain of 4 properties that obscures the underlying attrition rate
evidence_items.rationale: Acquisition masking attrition in net growth metrics is a critical adverse retention visibility signal. customer_retention; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: advertising spend is being increased to maintain acquisition volume rather than investigating why properties are leaving
evidence_items.rationale: Increasing acquisition investment without investigating the attrition cause is an adverse resource allocation signal. process_maturity.

evidence_items.finding: property management; 62 properties; 14 lost, 18 won (net +4); 23% attrition; owner attributes to market; advertising spend increasing
Surface signal (not root cause): net gain of 4 properties over 12 months creates the appearance of a growing business
evidence_items.rationale: Net portfolio growth is the primary misleading signal — 23% attrition masked by 29% acquisition creates the false appearance of healthy performance.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): landlords selling investment properties is a real and plausible market condition
evidence_items.rationale: Market condition attribution is a misleading external signal when the attrition rate has not been systematically analysed.

validation_notes: SIM-13-006 is SUPPORTED via customer_retention_erosion. 23% annual attrition masked by acquisition maps to customer retention erosion. No must_identify vocabulary.
